Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The umpires have paved their way to the center of the field. Followed by the players of Pakistan, to take their respective fielding positions. Shaheen Afridi will start with the new ball. Pathum Nissanka will take the strike, with the debutant, Kamil Mishara. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The stage is now set for the second half of the match. With 299 runs on the board, Pakistan have a humongous total to defend, and the focus now shifts to their bowling attack. The Lankan batters will look to build on a strong partnership to successfully chase the target. Also, due might be a factor as Charith Asalanka said at the time of toss. Will Sri Lanka's batting unit overcome the total, or will Pakistan's bowlers defend the total successfully? We shall find out soon. Chase is coming up shortly...

Wanindu Hasaranga, the pick of the bowlers for Sri Lanka, is up for a quick chat. He says that they started well with the ball but credits Salman and Talat for the way they batted after four wickets. Adds that the wicket looks good and he thinks they can chase this down. Mentions that he is the main wicket-taker for his team, and his plan is always to attack the stumps. Says that he doesn't change much between formats and just tries to stick to his strengths.

After the fall of the second wicket, Hasaranga got two more wickets in quick succession and Pakistan were 95 for 4 wickets in the 24th over. But the partnership between Salman Agha and Hussain Talat changed the narrative of the game. Talat got a golden lifeline at the early stage of his inning. Due to a wrong decision of the umpire, he stayed alive on the pitch, and Sri Lanka didn't have any reviews left in their bank to challenge. Talat made sure he cashed it out well and scored 62 runs off 63 deliveries. On the other end of the pitch, Salman Agha kept his blissful stroke play and got his deserved century. Credit to Mohammad Nawaz as his quickfire helped his side to post 300 target on the scoreboard.

The Pakistan openers, even after starting their inning with caution, fell under the brilliance of Ashitha Fernando, who drew the first blood on behalf of the team. With that first wicket, Pakistan fell on their back foot and the bowlers of Sri Lanka made it sure that they kept the pressure on their opposition. However, Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman eased the situation, but the boundaries were dried up. As soon as the latter started taking the authority, Wanindu Hasaranga stepped up and put an end to the danger hovering over Lanka.

What an inning we just witnessed! In the first half of the innings, we all thought that Sri Lanka held the grasp of the game, but one partnership changed everything. As a wise man said, anything can happen in the game of cricket. Hands down to Salman Agha for his master stroke, scoring 105 runs off 87 deliveries and helping his side to put up a total of 299 on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! Pakistan are hosting Sri Lanka in an ODI series after 6 years. The crowd has come in numbers for this first game. We can now see the Lankan players spread out and take their respective field positions. Fakhar Zaman and ​​​​Saim Ayub are the two openers for the Men in Green. Asitha Fernando has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play....

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for the respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first followed by that of Pakistan.

Mike Hesson, the Head Coach of Pakistan, is up for a quick chat. He says that he is pleased with the performance of the team as they recently won the series against the Proteas. Adds that they are trying to be better each day, as they have to work a lot to be at the top in ODIs. Ends up by saying that the track for this game looks a bit balance than the usual Rawalpindi wicket.

PITCH REPORT - Waqar Younis is along side the pitch with his insights. He reckons that the pitch looks great, and despite not relying on stats, he notes that 336 has been successfully chased here. He believes it's a pitch where you'd want to chase, given its history of big scores. The grass and cracks might play a role in the early overs, but after that, it should be a batting-friendly surface. He also mentions that the pitch might be slow initially, but under the lights with dew, hitting through the line should become easier.

Shaheen Afridi, the captain of Pakistan, says that they would have liked to bowl first as well due to the few. Adds that this is a high-scoring ground and they have to bat well. Says that Abrar Ahmed and Mohammad Wasim are not feeling well.

Charith Asalanka, skipper of Sri Lanka, says that it's a decent pitch but dew might come later in the innings, therefore they have opted to bowl first. Says that Wanindu Hasaranga returns to the ODI side and Kamil Mishara will make his debut in this game.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Salman Agha, Hussain Talat, Mohammad Nawaz, Shaheen Afridi (C), Faheem Ashraf, Haris Rauf, Naseem Shah.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kamil Mishara (On Debut), Kusal Mendis (WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka (C), Janith Liyanage, Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Maheesh Theekshana, Asitha Fernando.
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

The series opener couldn't get more exciting, as Pakistan will aim for a commanding series victory, but the Lankans are in formidable form as well. The weather is sunny and warm, most ideal for a game of cricket. So get ready folks, as the action will begin in no time. Till then, stay tuned for toss and team updates!

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, enter with confidence of their own, having enjoyed a positive run this year with seven wins in ten ODIs according to recent stats. Charith Asalanka and Pathum Nissanka have been among the main batting threats, while Asitha Fernando and Wanindu Hasaranga bring punch to their bowling attack. Sri Lanka will aim to play a fearless top-order, disrupt Pakistan’s rhythm early, and use their spin-battery to challenge the home side.

Pakistan will arrive with momentum and some standout performers. Fresh from a 2-1 series win over the Proteas, the Men in Green have their batting in decent shape with Salman Agha and Saim Ayub emerging as sharp operators in the white-ball format. Abrar Ahmed has been leading the spin attack effectively. Pakistan will be high in confidence and will look forward to starting the first encounter of the series on a high note.

Hello and welcome to all the cricket fans joining us for the build-up of today's matchup! Today kicks off the first of the three-match ODI series between Pakistan and Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. The stadium is all set to offer a high-stakes contest as Pakistan looks to extend home dominance, and Sri Lanka seeks to assert themselves on foreign soil.
... MATCHDAY ...

A fresh chapter of subcontinental rivalry is set to unfold in Rawalpindi, where Pakistan and Sri Lanka lock horns in the first ODI of what promises to be a gripping three-match series. Pakistan come in high on confidence after a 2-1 triumph over South Africa at home, but not without concerns - Babar Azam’s lean patch continues as he has now gone 82 innings without an international century, while Mohammad Rizwan too has struggled for consistency. Yet, the form of Saim Ayub, Mohammad Nawaz, and Salman Agha offers reassurance, each having chipped in with crucial runs in recent outings. The pace trio of Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, and Naseem Shah are back operating together, and their early breakthroughs could define Pakistan’s rhythm in the series. Adding to that, Abrar Ahmed’s spin threat gives the bowling attack a dangerous edge in the middle overs, while Faheem Ashraf’s ability to chip in with key wickets, along with handy runs down the order, and Hussain Talat’s explosive lower-order hitting add balance and depth to the side, making Pakistan a formidable outfit at home. For Sri Lanka, it’s a return to ODI cricket after nearly three months, and they’ll need to find their feet quickly in these conditions. Charith Asalanka’s leadership, along with Wanindu Hasaranga’s all-round brilliance, will be pivotal in shaping their fortunes. Pathum Nissanka, in sublime touch over the past couple of years, holds the key at the top, while Kusal and Kamindu Mendis add much-needed solidity in the middle order. The pace pairing of Asitha Fernando and Dushmantha Chameera brings control and aggression, and Maheesh Theekshana’s mystery spin could be the X-factor. Pakistan lead the overall head-to-head comfortably with 93 wins in 157 ODIs, including a 2-0 home series triumph when the Lankans last visited here in 2019, and the hosts will be eager to repeat history, while Sri Lanka will look to flip the script this time around. Whose side are you on?
